scope: Extend P6-G whole-write transaction coverage for standalone ATTRIB/SEQEND INSERTs across intermediate legacy DXF writer revisions AC1018 and AC1021.

source.kind: deterministic locally-authored records generated during the test
source.profile: One INSERT with two non-MTEXT ATTRIB children, distinct handles, tags, text and geometry; AC1018 and AC1021 output, each in ASCII and Binary DXF.

implementation.change: Expanded the standalone attributed INSERT transaction selector to AC1015, AC1018, AC1021 and AC1024. This follow-up closes the intermediate AC1018/AC1021 version points between the earlier AC1015/AC1024 coverage.
implementation.method: Calibrate reached allocations in a successful write, then inject std::bad_alloc at every reached offset. Verify export failure, sentinel destination preservation, unchanged caller INSERT/ATTRIB fields, no staged output, same-codec retry to byte-identical output, and fresh typed readback of both attributes.

validation.focusedCTest: ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_legacy_attributed_insert_allocation_transaction$' --output-on-failure: PASS 1/1 in 5.66 seconds; selector runs all four legacy revisions.
validation.diffCheck: PASS: git diff --check on the implementation, plan and receipt paths

limitations: Generated AC1018 and AC1021 transaction evidence only; producer interoperability and native consumer behavior are not qualified.
Only one INSERT with two standalone ATTRIB children is covered; other compound-record field profiles remain in P6-G inventory.

planImpact.completedSlice: AC1018 and AC1021 standalone ATTRIB/SEQEND ASCII and Binary allocation rollback, same-codec retry and typed readback.
planImpact.remainingP6G: Continue with distinct public-writer overloads, other compound-record variants, variable-size OBJECTS builders, and uncovered caller-state combinations.
